comparator.name: Actuarial Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum accounts for the full 180 ECTS as ten compulsory 6-ECTS courses in year 1, ten compulsory 6-ECTS courses in year 2, a 30-ECTS free-choice first semester in year 3, and five compulsory 6-ECTS components in the final semester. The programme offers identical Dutch- and English-track content; the generic registry target does not specify a language track, so no route is selected. The 30-ECTS My Semester remains genuine open choice rather than being populated with invented courses.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics & quantitative risk
alternatives.labelReason: The completed schedule has a genuine financial-economics and quantitative-methods spine, including probability, econometrics, finance, programming and optimisation. The label deliberately says quantitative risk rather than Actuarial Science because UCR does not offer the programme’s insurance- and pension-specific actuarial sequence.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines economics, accounting, banking and finance with calculus, linear algebra, probability, econometrics, programming, databases, machine learning, optimisation and responsible decision-making. It supports quantitative analysis of financial uncertainty but does not reproduce the comparator’s dedicated life-insurance, pension, reserving, stochastic-life-model or actuarial-thesis sequence.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

selection.assessment: All fourteen direct programme-interest rows belong to the same tightly integrated actuarial generator: mathematical and statistical risk modelling applied to finance, insurance, pensions and organisational decisions. UCR can form one coherent finance, economics and quantitative-risk curriculum, but it has no separate actuarial, insurance or pension sequence from which to build a second substantively distinct 24-course pathway. Additional variants would therefore be arbitrary substitutions rather than evidence-led alternatives.

blocks: Both provide calculus foundations, though UCR Mathematical Methods is broader and less proof-intensive.
Advanced Calculus supplies multivariable calculus and differential-equation methods but is not identical to the comparator course.
Both provide probability, estimation and inference foundations; the comparator continues through two further compulsory probability-statistics courses.
Research Methods & Statistics adds applied statistical design and inference, but does not reproduce the comparator’s second probability-theory course.
The comparator requires a second, advanced linear-algebra course; UCR has no separate successor to Linear Algebra.
The comparator requires a third advanced probability and mathematical-statistics course; no second UCR probability course supplies that progression.
Introduction to Economics supplies both micro- and macroeconomic foundations; this row aligns it only with the comparator’s introductory microeconomics component.
Microeconomics & Behavior provides formal choice-under-uncertainty and market analysis, but not the comparator’s full mathematical-economics scope.
Accounting & Corporate Finance supplies corporate-finance and financial-statement foundations.
Money, Banking & Finance overlaps with financial markets and quantitative financial decisions but is broader and less mathematical than the comparator course.
Both develop regression-based econometric analysis; the comparator continues with a second compulsory econometrics course.
Database Management Systems contributes structured-data methods but does not replace the actuarial content of the comparator’s introductory course.
UCR has one dedicated Econometrics course and no separate compulsory successor at the comparator’s depth.
UCR has research-methods courses but no dedicated Actuarial Science and Mathematical Finance seminar.
No UCR course teaches life-insurance mathematics, premium valuation or pension reserving.
No UCR course supplies the comparator’s dedicated actuarial Risk Theory course.
The comparator’s 30-ECTS My Semester is genuine open choice and is not forced into a one-to-one UCR course match.
UCR Accounting & Corporate Finance is already aligned with general first-year finance and does not teach life-insurance accounting.
No UCR course teaches stochastic life-insurance models.
UCR has course-based research projects but no independent Actuarial Science thesis research component.
UCR has academic-skills training but no separate actuarial thesis-skills component.

notes.text: UvA Actuarial Science has a cumulative specialist sequence in life-insurance mathematics, risk theory, stochastic life-insurance models, insurance accounting and actuarial research, followed by the wider master and post-master route toward the certified-actuary title. UCR can provide a coherent finance, economics, probability, econometrics and data-science pathway, but it does not offer those actuarial disciplines or an actuarial thesis. The included curriculum is therefore an academically related quantitative-risk alternative, not an Actuarial Science degree or professional actuarial pathway.
